Doc fields (`tenantScoped` reason, `idempotent`, `retryPolicy`, `poisonMessageHandling`, `retentionPolicyTouched`) are presence + >=10-char-prose verified only; their accuracy is a human review concern (SC3), same trust level as route-policy-manifest.json's `handlerAuthReason`. Per the worker-runtime-invariants plan C5, `sweepBounds` (every `rawSql: true` entry) and `runtimeBounds` (audit-outbox-worker only) are additionally mechanized: every DELETE/UPDATE write statement the shared SQL scanner (scripts/checks/lib/sql-scan.mjs) reads in an entry's modules must be single-row by its table's primary key, capped by a materialized key set (`WITH <cte> AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT <keys> ... LIMIT n) ... WHERE (<keys>) IN (SELECT <keys> FROM <cte>)` as a top-level AND conjunct), or covered by exactly one tight, used `sweepBounds.exemptions[]` entry, and `runtimeBounds` values are cross-checked against the literal constants in src/lib/constants/audit/audit.ts and the `@default(8)` maxAttempts lines in prisma/schema.prisma.

tenantScoped.reason: Every claim/deliver/reap/purge transaction sets bypass_rls + app.tenant_id=NIL_UUID + its grant's tables via setBypassGucs (audit-outbox-worker.ts) and then operates per-row using the row's own tenant_id column (e.g. deliverRow, deliverRowWithChain) -- it is a system-wide sweep by role privilege, but every write is attributed to the row's own tenant.

audit-outbox-worker.idempotent: claimBatch (via claimOutboxBatchInTx) picks at most batchSize PENDING ids in a MATERIALIZED CTE with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and flips only those rows (re-checking status='PENDING'), so concurrent workers claim each row exactly once; deliverRow/deliverRowWithChain INSERT INTO audit_logs ... ON CONFLICT (outbox_id) DO NOTHING so a re-delivered row after a crash is a no-op (audit-outbox-worker.ts claimOutboxBatchInTx, deliverRow, deliverRowWithChain).
audit-outbox-worker.retryPolicy: recordError computes exponential backoff with full jitter (computeBackoffMs + withFullJitter, audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError) and reschedules via next_retry_at; a row exceeding max_attempts transitions to FAILED (dead-letter) instead of retrying forever (audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError, isDead branch).
audit-outbox-worker.poisonMessageHandling: Rows at/over max_attempts are marked FAILED and an AUDIT_OUTBOX_DEAD_LETTER event is written directly to audit_logs (bypassing the outbox, to avoid recursion) in the same transaction via writeDirectAuditLogInTx (audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError, isDead branch); reapStuckRows separately reaps at most REAP_BATCH_SIZE PROCESSING rows stuck past PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS per pass, dead-lettering those already at max_attempts (audit-outbox-worker.ts reapStuckRows, reapStuckRowsInTx).

exemptions.reason: Anchor advance is single-row by PK (WHERE tenant_id = $3, tenant_id is audit_chain_anchors' primary key); not a multi-row sweep.

tenantScoped.reason: The NOBYPASSRLS passwd_retention_gc_worker role runs each globalDelete / per-tenant sweep entry in a transaction whose bypass_rls is set by the module-private dispatcher (sweep.ts inSweepTx; each sweep asserts it) to span all tenants under existing RLS policies, but every EXPIRY_AUDIT_PROVENANCE / PER_TENANT_FN / PER_TENANT_TRASH / PER_TENANT_AGE entry enumerates or attributes rows by their own tenant_id (sweep.ts sweepAuditLogs, sweepPerTenantAge, sweepTrashEntry) -- a deliberate all-tenant blast radius (registry.ts, the globalDelete field doc), never a cross-tenant write of one tenant's data into another. The team key prune runs in one bypass transaction across all teams and writes its TEAM_MEMBER_KEY_PRUNED audit under each pruned row's own tenant_id (sweep.ts sweepTeamMemberKeys).

retention-gc-worker.idempotent: Each EXPIRY/EXPIRY_GUARDED/EXPIRY_AUDIT_PROVENANCE DELETE is batch-bounded by a MATERIALIZED key-set CTE (WITH picked AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT keys ... LIMIT $1) DELETE ... WHERE (keys) IN (SELECT keys FROM picked)) keyed off cutoffColumn < now(), so a re-run after a crash simply finds fewer (or zero) newly-expired rows -- no duplicate side effects (sweep.ts sweepExpiryEntry, sweepGuardedExpiryEntry, sweepAuditProvenanceEntry). sweepAuditLogs routes through the audit_log_purge SECURITY DEFINER function which is itself a plain bounded DELETE (registry.ts, the PER_TENANT_FN audit_logs entry; sweep.ts sweepAuditLogs). sweepTeamMemberKeys calls the team_member_key_prune SECURITY DEFINER function, which locks the candidate teams (SKIP LOCKED) and then deletes at most p_batch unreferenced (team, version) pairs, so a re-run finds only what is still unreferenced; sweepOrphanBlobs deletes objects by exact key, and a repeated delete of a gone object is a no-op (sweep.ts sweepTeamMemberKeys; sweep-blob-orphans.ts).
retention-gc-worker.retryPolicy: No per-row retry/backoff: sweepOnce catches each registry entry's error individually (INV-C4b), logs {table, code} only, records counts[table]=-1, and continues to the next entry -- the NEXT scheduled sweep tick (fixed intervalMs, no backoff) naturally retries the same cutoff-based query (sweep.ts sweepOnce, the per-entry registry loop).
retention-gc-worker.poisonMessageHandling: There is no per-row poison-message concept (bulk cutoff-based DELETE, not a per-item queue); a systematically failing entry (e.g. a bad identifier) is caught per-tick, logged with {table, code}, and left for the next tick -- the boot-time validateRegistry() call fails closed (throws) before the loop starts if any registry entry has an invalid identifier or missing globalDelete flag, so malformed entries never reach runtime processing (index.ts validateRegistry, called from createWorker).
retentionPolicyTouched: attachments (external blob objects no row references; rows untouched)

audit-anchor-publisher.$modules-note: anchor-published-state.ts holds the destination side of the publication decision (what is published is read from the primary destination) and opens no database connection. The destination implementations under src/lib/audit/anchor-destinations/ are not listed: they touch no database either, and github-release-destination.ts carries the HTTP method DELETE in string literals (its one removal of an asset-name reservation that never received content), which the sweepBounds scanner would read as a write statement it cannot judge.

tenantScoped.reason: Every runCadence transaction (the unlocked read at the start of runBounded, claimAttempt, the publish transaction, and persistPause) sets the AUDIT_ANCHOR_PUBLISH bypass grant with app.tenant_id=SYSTEM_TENANT_ID (setBypassGucs) to read every auditChainEnabled tenant's anchor row in one cadence run, but the manifest it builds and the lastPublishedAt / publishPausedUntil updates it writes are always partitioned per tenantId (AnchorRow[] per tenant; updateMany scoped to coveredTenantIds -- the anchor rows whose tenant tag is in the stored manifest -- in runBounded, and to the failed run's pauseTenantIds in persistPause) -- a system-wide read, never a cross-tenant data write.

audit-anchor-publisher.idempotent: One manifest object per cadence boundary, decided from the primary destination (config.destinations[0]; buildDestinationsFromEnv orders S3, then GitHub Releases, then the filesystem), not from a database row. Each run (runBounded) lists the primary and builds a PublishedState (publishedStateFromListing): the latest manifest key is read and verified by readVerifiedManifest -- a key under the own kid with the own key, one under a foreign kid with public-keys/<kid>.pub read from the same destination; verify binds the header's kid to the key; the key's date must be the UTC date of anchoredAt. decide() then applies, first match. Fail closed, before any write: a list or read error (<destination>_READ_FAILED:<code>); a latest manifest that does not verify (CADENCE_FAILED:PUBLISHED_OBJECT_UNVERIFIABLE); one that is not of this chain location (assertOfThisChain) -- a version 2 manifest whose chainLocation is not chainLocationFor(primary.location) (PUBLISHED_OBJECT_FOREIGN_LOCATION), or a version 1 manifest, which names no location, whose date is not the date of the published high-water (LEGACY_MANIFEST_UNSETTLED); one dated after the wall clock's boundary (PUBLISHED_OBJECT_AHEAD); MAX(audit_chain_anchors.last_published_at) over ALL anchor rows (publishedHighWater) mapping past the wall clock's boundary (LAST_PUBLISHED_AHEAD_OF_CLOCK) or past the latest manifest's date (DESTINATION_BEHIND_DATABASE); a latest manifest under a foreign kid while a manifest key named with the own kid exists (LATEST_UNDER_RETIRED_KEY). Skip (skipped_already_published): the latest manifest is dated after the boundary (also logs audit-anchor-publisher.stale_boundary, alarmed on AWS); it is the boundary's own but not signed under the own kid with the own deploymentId (published_by_other_identity, one PUBLISHED_BY_OTHER_IDENTITY row per boundary per publisher instance); it is the boundary's own, ours, and last_published_at reaches the boundary. Adopt: the boundary's own, ours, not recorded -- the stored bytes are mirrored and recorded and nothing is signed. Otherwise publish, with the latest manifest as previousManifest. last_published_at can therefore make a run refuse or adopt again, never skip. The decision runs before claimAttempt and again inside the publish transaction under the lock. Every write is create-only (AnchorDestination.create: S3 IfNoneMatch '*' with 412 read as 'exists', filesystem link() with EEXIST, the GitHub asset name); a create answered 'exists' reads the stored object back through readVerifiedManifest, holds it to assertOfThisChain as the latest manifest is, and adopts it when it is ours, so a retry after a lost commit or a crash stores no second version of the key. Secondaries are given the primary's bytes (mirrorToSecondaries); one that already holds other bytes at the key fails the run (<destination>_MIRROR_DIVERGED). The value written to last_published_at is the wall clock clamped into [boundary, boundary + cadence) (publishTime), on the anchor rows whose tenant tag is in the stored manifest, so it always maps to the boundary whose object exists. Serialization: every run sets SET LOCAL lock_timeout (setLockTimeout, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s) and then takes the BLOCKING pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('audit-anchor-publish')) (advisoryXactLock, ADVISORY_LOCK_KEY); a wait past the timeout raises SQLSTATE 55P03, read through pgErrorCode (isLockNotAvailable) and returned as lock_held, which is not a failure. The boundary is the one createAnchorScheduler armed the timer for, not the clock at publish time, so it alone fixes the artifact key (buildManifestArtifactKey) and anchoredAt. A manifest is built as format version 2 (buildManifest), bound to the primary's location; secondaries hold those bytes. The system_settings rows audit_anchor_last_published_boundary and audit_anchor_previous_manifest that earlier releases decided from are read and written by nothing and are deleted by the migration 20261115000000_remove_audit_anchor_legacy_settings. A wait past the lock timeout is lock_held only while the primary holds nothing for the boundary; once it does, the same SQLSTATE is a failed run. ensureDeploymentIdMatch is NOT a single-owner lock: it pins DEPLOYMENT_ID in system_settings (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) so a publisher configured for another deployment refuses to boot (DeploymentIdMismatchError); a second instance with the same DEPLOYMENT_ID boots and is serialized by the lock and the create-only write. On ECS the service runs at most one task (desired_count = min(1, worker_desired_count), deployment_maximum_percent = 100, deployment_minimum_healthy_percent = 0), so a deploy stops the old task before starting the new one.
audit-anchor-publisher.retryPolicy: Two layers. In process: createAnchorScheduler awaits one run for the current boundary at boot, then re-arms a setTimeout computed from the wall clock after every run (no setInterval). A failed run at any stage, and a lock_held run (isRetryable), is retried for the SAME boundary every ANCHOR_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS (15 min), at most ANCHOR_MAX_RETRIES_PER_BOUNDARY (3) times per process and only while the retry falls at least ANCHOR_RETRY_STOP_BEFORE_NEXT_MS (30 min) before the next boundary; when either bound stops it, it logs audit-anchor-publisher.retries_exhausted with reason count or window_closed and waits. A lock_held retry whose lock holder published finds the boundary's manifest at the primary destination and returns skipped_already_published. That in-process bound is the only one on a failure before claimAttempt writes the count (the tenants read failing, the database unreachable, a fail-closed decision at the run's first look at the primary), which the persisted cap never sees. upload_cap_reached is not retried; it waits for the next boundary or the next boot run. Persisted cap: claimAttempt counts every run whose first decision was publish or adopt in system_settings.audit_anchor_upload_attempts ({boundary, count}; findUnique + Prisma upsert under the advisory lock) in its OWN transaction, committed before the publish transaction opens, so neither a rollback nor a crash after the create resets it and a crash-looping task cannot keep reaching the destinations; a run with no chain-enabled tenant that has an anchor row (chainEnabledTenants) returns skipped_no_tenants without counting, and a run that skips at its first decision is not counted either. A run whose count exceeds AUDIT_ANCHOR_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP (3) writes nothing and returns upload_cap_reached. A stored count that does not parse (JSON or schema; parseUploadAttempts) is overwritten in the same claim transaction with {boundary: this boundary, count: AUDIT_ANCHOR_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP + 1}, so the run reports upload_cap_reached (fail-closed for that boundary) and the next boundary counts 1 again. A commit lost after every destination holds the object rolls the publish transaction back and writes no pause (commit_failed_after_upload); the retry finds the stored object and adopts it (published with adopted: true) -- it creates nothing, so the key keeps one version. After a published outcome backfillMirrors copies to each secondary at most AUDIT_ANCHOR_MIRROR_BACKFILL_MAX (7) manifest keys the primary holds and it lacks, newest first; a failure logs audit-anchor-publisher.mirror_backfill_failed, changes no outcome, and is taken up again by the next publishing run. Bounds: lock wait 10 s; ALL destination I/O of one run -- listings, reads, creates and the mirror backfill -- 60 s as a whole (DEFAULT_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS; DestinationBound, one AbortController armed at the run's first destination call, plus untilAborted), reported as UPLOAD_TIMEOUT under the operation it interrupted; each transaction 90 s (DEFAULT_TX_TIMEOUT_MS). ECS stopTimeout is 120 s, and SIGTERM stops the scheduler arming and waits for the in-flight run (AnchorScheduler.stop) before the pool is closed (createPublisherLifecycle); a signal during boot first waits for the boot to settle and then exits 0, never as boot_failed.
audit-anchor-publisher.poisonMessageHandling: There is no per-item queue to poison; the unit is a cadence boundary. Each failed run (fail) logs audit-anchor-publisher.cadence_failed and writes one AUDIT_ANCHOR_PUBLISH_FAILED row through emitAudit, which never throws and sends a failed outbox write to the dead-letter logger -- per boundary, at most 3 counted runs across restarts (one row each) plus the one cap row; a failure before the count is written is uncounted and bounded instead by the scheduler, at most 1 + ANCHOR_MAX_RETRIES_PER_BOUNDARY runs per boundary per process start. The poison analogue is a fail-closed state of the primary destination or of last_published_at (PUBLISHED_OBJECT_UNVERIFIABLE, PUBLISHED_OBJECT_FOREIGN_LOCATION, LEGACY_MANIFEST_UNSETTLED, PUBLISHED_OBJECT_AHEAD, LAST_PUBLISHED_AHEAD_OF_CLOCK, DESTINATION_BEHIND_DATABASE, LATEST_UNDER_RETIRED_KEY): it fails every run, of every boundary, until an operator resets it (docs/operations/audit-anchor-rotation-runbook.md, 'Fail-closed reasons and their resets'); nothing is written to a destination meanwhile, and the cadence_failed alarm fires on each run. An upload failure -- a create failing at the primary or a secondary, a secondary that cannot be read back, or one holding other bytes (<destination>_MIRROR_DIVERGED) -- also persists publish_paused_until on the tenants the manifest covers until the next boundary (persistPause, its own transaction after the rollback); that pause is held by the audit-outbox worker, which stops advancing those tenants' chains, and does not hold publishing -- every chain-enabled tenant with an anchor row is published, and a successful publish clears it. The first run past the cap logs audit-anchor-publisher.upload_cap_reached (alarmed) and writes one UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP_REACHED failure row for the boundary (UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_COUNT_UNREADABLE, with countUnreadable: true on the log line, when the stored count did not parse); later runs for that boundary log only. Rows written after the commit of a published outcome, detection only: AUDIT_ANCHOR_KEY_ROTATED when the manifest's kid differs from the one it chains to, and AUDIT_ANCHOR_PUBLISH_FAILED rows OWN_PUBLIC_KEY_NOT_ARCHIVED, MULTIPLE_MANIFESTS_FOR_DATE, TENANT_DROPPED_FROM_MANIFEST, CHAIN_SEQ_REGRESSION and EPOCH_CHANGED (the last three against the manifest the published one chains to: the one in hand on a fresh publish, and on an adopted publish the one its previousManifest names, read back from the primary by namedPrevious and held to the sha256 it carries and to this chain's location -- PREVIOUS_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE_FOR_COMPARISON when that fails; each of the four carries comparedArtifactKey, the manifest the row is about). A run that fails once the primary holds the boundary's manifest (stage upload with the object stored, or after_upload) writes those four comparison rows for that manifest itself, after its failure row and inside the run's destination bound (the catch of runBounded: predecessorOf, comparisonEmits), so a manifest that is stored and never settled has been compared by the run that stored it; a retry repeats them, at most the attempt cap. A manifest stored by runs that all failed after the primary held it (a secondary failure, COMMIT_FAILED_AFTER_UPLOAD, a stage-upload failure, or the attempt cap) is compared again, which covers a run killed before it wrote its rows: the next published outcome, after its mirror backfill, walks back from the manifest it chains to through every manifest dated after the published high-water it decided from (unsettledEmits; all of them when no anchor row has a last_published_at), reads each one's previous manifest through namedPrevious inside the run's destination bound, and writes the same four rows with comparedArtifactKey naming the unsettled manifest; a manifest dated on the high-water's date is settled and not compared again. The walk compares at most AUDIT_ANCHOR_UNSETTLED_WALK_MAX (7) manifests; when an unsettled one lies past them it stops and writes one UNSETTLED_WALK_TRUNCATED row (count, comparedArtifactKey the last manifest compared). A published outcome, and a run that fails once the primary holds the manifest, also write one GENESIS_AFTER_EARLIER_MANIFESTS row (genesisEmits) when the manifest the run adopted, or the one its manifest chains to, names no previousManifest although the primary lists a manifest key dated before it; comparedArtifactKey names that manifest, and a skip writes nothing. A boundary that was never recorded is reported by the next publish as MISSING_PRIOR_CADENCE_PUBLICATION (audit-anchor-publisher.missing_prior_cadence): its row is written only when that run publishes, so a failing run's retries do not repeat it.

audit-chain-verify-worker.$modules-note: DB logic is inlined in the script itself (no src/workers counterpart) -- mechanical greps (rawSql/destructive/emitsAudit/usesSecurityDefiner) run against this file directly, per plan review S1.

tenantScoped.reason: runTick enumerates ALL tenants under the named SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_TENANT_LOOKUP bypass grant (tenants carries the same RLS policy as every other table since migration 20261022000000_tenants_rls) and calls verifyTenantChain once per tenantId, and the underlying query filters WHERE tenant_id = $1 (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts runTick, verifyTenantChain) -- a system-wide read loop, but each verification pass is scoped to a single tenant's chain: via its own withTenantRls context, or for the __system__ sentinel (which withTenantRls refuses) under the AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_SENTINEL_READ bypass grant, with the returned rows asserted to belong to it.

audit-chain-verify-worker.idempotent: Verification is read-only (SELECT ... ORDER BY chain_seq ASC, no writes) and re-walks the same rows deterministically every tick, so re-running never mutates state and always reproduces the same ok/firstTamperedSeq result for an unchanged chain (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:68-121).
audit-chain-verify-worker.retryPolicy: No retry semantics: a per-tenant verify failure is caught, logged ("tenant=%s verify threw", as errorLogFields plus the worker's own precondition message), and the loop continues to the next tenant; the NEXT hourly tick (fixed TICK_INTERVAL_MS, no backoff) re-attempts the same tenant from scratch (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:130-173,208-215).
audit-chain-verify-worker.poisonMessageHandling: Not applicable -- there is no queue or per-row claim, only a full per-tenant re-scan every tick; a tamper finding is reported via CHAIN_VERIFY_FAILED console logging with hysteresis (re-alert only on clean-to-failed transition or every 24h while failed, audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:145-163) rather than any dead-letter mechanism.
